targetWords.definition: If something or someone is absurd, they are ridiculous.
targetWords.example: That group o f people making animal noises sounds completely absurd.

targetWords.definition: Anemia is a blood condition that causes a person to be pale and tired.
targetWords.example: When she first developed anemia, she became tired often.

targetWords.definition: The aristocracy is the highest class of people in certain societies.
targetWords.example: Most members o f the aristocracy were very well-fed.

targetWords.definition: An aristocrat is a person who is of the highest class in certain societies.
targetWords.example: The aristocrat did not need a job because his fam ily was wealthy.

targetWords.definition: Attire is nice or special clothing.
targetWords.example: Everyone wore their best attire to the president's daughter's wedding. craze [kreiz] n.

targetWords.definition: -» Wearing bright red socks was a craze when I was in high school.
targetWords.example: Wearing bright red socks was a craze when I was in high school.

targetWords.definition: To enlarge something means to make it bigger.
targetWords.example: The classrooms were enlarged over the summer to make room for more students.

targetWords.definition: An excess is an amount of something that is more than needed or wanted.
targetWords.example: Because it never got cold that winter, many stores had an excess o f coats.

targetWords.definition: If something is feminine, then it has qualities that are commonly related to women.
targetWords.example: Many o f the older people thought his long hair made him look too feminine. hallmark [h5:lma:rk] n.

targetWords.definition: —►Different types o f pasta and tomato sauces are hallmarks of Italian food.

targetWords.definition: A pad is a thick piece of soft material used to protect or clean things.
targetWords.example: Football players wear shoulder pads to keep them safe.

targetWords.definition: If something is predominant, then it is the most important, common or strongest.
targetWords.example: Before cars were invented, horses were the predominant method o f travel.

targetWords.definition: If someone or something is reputable, then they have a good reputation.
targetWords.example: The service from the less than reputable company made her angry.

targetWords.definition: Rouge is a red powder or cream used as makeup on the cheeks or lips.
targetWords.example: Even when she didn't wear rouge, her cheeks appeared red.

targetWords.definition: To signify means to be a symbol of something.
targetWords.example: A red octagon is used to signify to stop. strap [straep] n.

targetWords.definition: —*■She put the strap o f her purse over her shoulder and walked out o f the door.

targetWords.definition: —►The laces o f his shoes were in such a tangle that he could not untie them.

targetWords.definition: Vanity is excessive pride or love of one' s own appearance or things one has done.
targetWords.example: Her vanity won't allow her to pass a m irror without looking at herself.

targetWords.definition: To vie for something means to compete against others for it.
targetWords.example: The three boys vied for the prize in the chemistry contest.

targetWords.definition: If something or someone is vulgar, then they are rude or lacking in style.
targetWords.example: Her vulgar behavior got her into trouble with her parents.

story.title: Dressed to Excess
story.passage:
If you traveled back in time to the 1700s in Europe, you would laugh when you saw how

the aristocracy dressed. Soon you'd realize, though, that the aristocrats of Europe were

very serious about their appearance.

The predominant style in women's attire was enormous

dresses. They were often three times larger than

the wearer. Ladies even used pads to enlarge

the appearance of their hips and shoulders. On

the other extreme, the aristocratic women made

their waists appear extremely thin. It took several maids

stretching fabric and pulling straps in order to get a

lady's waist to the proper thinness. These ladies

could barely breathe and often fainted.

Pale skin was also a craze, yet this too was

done in excess. One could not simply be pale.

Instead, she needed to look as if she had

anemia. In order to look paler, ladies actually

cut themselves daily, so they would

bleed.

The hairstyles, however,

were the hallmark of

women's fashion. These

stood a meter high on the

ladies' heads. The columns

of hair were a ridiculous tangle

of wigs, jewels, flowers, and even

stuffed birds.

Men's fashion was similarly absurd. Today it

would probably seem very feminine. Reputable men

wore wigs of long curly hair. Their shoes had large

soles or high heels so that they could walk high

above the filth on the streets. Furthermore, just like

the ladies, the men wore lipstick and put rouge on

their cheeks.

Their clothes were brightly colored, often purple

and pink. They were made from the finest of fabrics and

decorated with jewels and lace. The men vied with one

another to see who wore the more expensive clothes, for the

clothing signified his wealth and status.

Both men and women spent huge amounts of money and time

on how they looked. Though such vanity would seem vulgar today,

three hundred years from now, the fashions of our time might also

seem completely ridiculous.
